Eight weeks for a team endurance challenge

Combine repeatable rucks, shared carries, practical communication and strength without trying to recreate an extreme event.

8 weeks · 4 training days · team · Updated 2026-11-24

Who this is for

For regular ruckers already comfortable with a 90–120 minute outing and basic strength work. Choose a partner or group that can agree on individual load, rest and withdrawal. No sleep deprivation, forced carries or punishment workouts.

A normal training week

Tuesday: 35–45 min easy ruck. Thursday: 30–40 min strength, using 2–3 sets of 6–10 squats, hinges, rows and controlled carries. Weekend: group session. One optional easy walk/cycle day; keep the day after group work easy.

Week by week

  1. 1: 75–90 min group outing; plan roles and check-ins.
  2. 2: 90 min; include 4 × 60 s shared carries with unloaded recovery.
  3. 3: 105 min; rehearse a route change and food stop.
  4. 4: 60–75 min; no demanding carries.
  5. 5: 120 min; include 4 × 90 s carry rotations, if week 2 was comfortable.
  6. 6: 135 min; keep shared carry volume unchanged; practise role handovers.
  7. 7: 75–90 min easy; reduce total work.
  8. 8: Chosen group challenge within established capacity; brief alternatives and finish together at a safe pace.

How to adjust

The group should learn to share work, not compete over who suffers most. Make every session adjustable. An actual event may require different preparation or more time; read its rules before choosing a target.

Put it into practice

For a useful reminder of why carrying and communication both matter, read Milton Memorial Tough field report.
